issues.description: The proposal guarantees that business logic will remain fully portable to any future infrastructure. However, the Client Matrix lists the 60-70% survival rate of Phase 1 work as low confidence. Stating this as a guaranteed fact violates the matrix constraints.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the guarantee of full portability. State that the architecture is designed to maximize reusability and reference the Open Questions section regarding the 60-70% survival target.

issues.description: The proposal explicitly commits to scoping the project strictly within the $300,000 budget cap. The budget cap is a contradicted item between Rita ($300k) and Sarah (up to $400k). Committing to one side in the pricing section prematurely resolves the contradiction.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the strict commitment to the $300,000 cap in the Pricing section. State that the final fixed fee will be determined once the budget range is clarified, pointing to the Open Questions section.

issues.description: The proposal definitively promises to deploy an operational production pilot by September 30. The feasibility of this Q3 deadline is a contradicted item (Marcus believes Q4 is realistic). Promising it as a certainty risks alienating the CTO.
issues.suggested_fix: Adjust the wording to state that the proposal outlines a targeted plan for a Q3 pilot, noting that final timeline feasibility will be confirmed with technical leadership during kickoff.

risks: Prematurely resolving contradicted items (budget and timeline) in the main proposal body risks alienating key stakeholders like Sarah and Marcus.
Overpromising on technical portability sets unrealistic expectations that conflict with the low-confidence 60-70% survival estimate.
